record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: In the radial-domain case Ω = B_r(0) for problem (II), namely -Δu + 1/u^α = λ u^p in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω, α > 0 (mainly α < 1), and 0 < p < 1, are there non-radial solutions even though the cited analysis only treats radial ones?

evidence.quote: Also we will consider problem (II): -Δu + 1/u^α = λ u^p in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, with 0 < α (mainly α < 1) and 0 < p < 1.
since the famous Gidas-Ni-Nirenberg theorem is not applicable, existence of non-radial solutions cannot be excluded.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_r(0)\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\ge 2$) denote the open ball of radius $r>0$ centered at the origin. Fix parameters $\alpha>0$ (mainly the case $0<\alpha<1$ is of interest), $0<p<1$, and $\lambda>0$, and consider the singular semilinear elliptic Dirichlet problem
$$
-\Delta u + \frac{1}{u^{\alpha}} = \lambda\, u^{p} \quad \text{in } B_r(0), \qquad u>0 \text{ in } B_r(0), \qquad u=0 \text{ on } \partial B_r(0).
$$
Because the absorption term $1/u^{\alpha}$ is singular where $u$ vanishes, the classical moving-plane / Gidas–Ni–Nirenberg symmetry argument is not directly applicable, so a priori non-radial positive solutions are not excluded. 

Question: Does this problem admit a positive (weak/classical, in an appropriate sense) solution $u:B_r(0)\to(0,\infty)$ that is not radially symmetric about the origin? Equivalently, determine whether every positive solution must be radially symmetric, or exhibit values of $N$, $r$, $\alpha\in(0,1)$, $p\in(0,1)$, and $\lambda>0$ for which a non-radial positive solution exists.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any work establishing either symmetry of all positive solutions or the existence of a non-radial positive solution for this specific singular absorption problem $-\Delta u + u^{-\alpha} = \lambda u^p$ on a ball with $0<\alpha<1$, $0<p<1$. The symmetry obstruction (failure of Gidas–Ni–Nirenberg due to the singular term) is widely acknowledged, and related literature on singular elliptic equations and non-radial bifurcation exists, but no resolution of this particular question was found.

status_evidence.title: Multiple nonradial solutions for a nonlinear elliptic problem with singular and decaying radial potential
status_evidence.snippet: Multiple nonradial solutions exist for related singular elliptic problems, illustrating that symmetry can fail in singular settings.
status_evidence.claim: Non-radial solutions are known in nearby singular elliptic problems, but not specifically for the absorption equation in question.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of solutions to singular p-Laplacian equations with subcritical nonlinearity
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness (and hence radial symmetry) results are available for some singular subcritical p-Laplacian problems on balls.
status_evidence.claim: Symmetry/uniqueness results in related singular problems do not cover the present equation with absorption $1/u^\alpha$ and source $\lambda u^p$.
